A bit of both. D12 is only Win10 compatible. Meaning that if you create a game that required D12 to run, you can only sell that to XboxOne and Win10 Users.

Gamers refusing to upgrade from 7 and 8/8.1 to Win10 because of privacy concerns, are stuck with D11.

Vulkan offers the same benefits, but is not restricted by OS. So long as you have hardware capable of running OpenGL ES 3.1 or OpenGL 4.X and above, and a driver which supports Vulkan, you can play a game which utilizes Vulkan.

Basically, if Vulkan proves as every bit as powerful as D12, developers will gravitate towards it for the larger customer base potential and the lower costs/development time involved in releasing a title for different OSes.
